blocks.heading: PGWP Vs the German Job-Seeker Visa

items.text: This is where the two countries diverge the most, and it is the part most agents summarise too quickly.
Masters graduates get a 3-year open work permit, regardless of whether the program was 1 or 2 years, following the rule change effective February 2024.
The PGWP is an open permit, meaning you can work for almost any employer in almost any role while you search, which lowers the pressure to land a perfect-fit job immediately.
This is the factor that should carry the most weight, and the one general "Canada vs Germany" articles skip the most.
Canada's English-only hiring market and large Toronto/Vancouver tech sector give you more roles without needing German.
Germany has a well-documented structural shortage of engineers.

visuals.heading: Language and Cultural Adjustment

items.text: English is the working language almost everywhere outside Quebec, so day-to-day life, job interviews, and networking do not require a second language.
A large existing Indian community across Toronto, Vancouver, and other cities means familiar food, festivals, and social groups are easy to find from day one.

The main adjustment cost is financial: higher rent, higher cost of living in the cities where most jobs concentrate, and a currency gap that makes even entry-level salaries feel tight against Canadian living costs at first.
